title: A marked tensor obstruction to four-dimensional disk embedding

issues.location: Appendix A / Prop. 4.? (formal-trace-comparison) and Sec. 4 'A model preserving the integrated trace'
issues.description: The whole algebraicity step (Thm 4.1: f = F∘φ with F algebraic) depends on the PTVV/Calaque -1-shifted form on Loc_G(Z)^fr being homotopic, as a full closed form, to the strict integrated trace form on the edge complex C. I only skimmed that comparison and did not verify it. If it fails, Lemma 4.3 gives no f − f' ∈ Jac^2, and Lemma 2.2 (Artin approximation and reduction to characteristic p) loses its algebraic separated potentials.
issues.evidence: Sec. 4: 'Both strict forms represent the same shifted closed-form class' is justified only by Prop. formal-trace-comparison (Appendix, ~370 lines built on Getzler/Dupont nerve constructions). I did not check it line by line. Everything downstream of it that I did check holds.

coverage: Read the introduction, Sec. 1 (geometric reduction), Sec. 2 (tensor obstruction, every lemma), Sec. 3 (edge potentials), Sec. 4 (algebraicity) and Sec. 5 (vertex data) in full. Skimmed the appendix trace comparison and the conclusion. Checks: (i) Sec. 1. The rim-torus/one-sided-contraction dual spheres: the η-sheet cancellation works because the difference loop is z_j, which bounds D_z in E. Embeddedness and framing of g_j hold. The Mayer–Vietoris dimension counts hold (ker R has dim 2p and is complementary to the kernel of the extra-letter evaluations). The slope argument (one original coordinate direction dies) and the deck-involution count of m active edges both hold. (ii) Sec. 3. The polarized complex C is self-dual: H^1(C)≅H^1(Y,T) pairs perfectly with H^2(C)≅H^2(Y), both of dim b1−1. The Jacobian ideal equals the curvature ideal. The boundary adjustment ε/2·tr(uv) cancels the boundary term. (iii) Sec. 4. The Cartan-homotopy argument giving f−f'∈J^2 and the flow that removes a J^2 error, including the formula for X_t, both check out. (iv) Sec. 5. Stokes gives S_P(H_P)∈I_P^2. The gradient matrix has full column rank. The correction lemmas hold, including the nilpotent version. Brunnian ⇒ law entries lie in J_ijk (an intersection of monomial ideals in disjoint variables), the cubic terms span by the Ad-span, Nakayama gives J_ijk=Q⊂I_P, and the polynomial b_i error estimates hold. (v) Sec. 2, in full: the Frobenius truncation invariance, integration by parts, nonvanishing of the graph-form pairing (I confirmed numerically that the socle coefficient is det(M)^{p−1}), the Koszul boundary identities, Künneth, kernel-support (ker of a tensor of maps over a field), the projection lemma (P chain map, P(K)⊂K∩Z, homotopy), [δ,B]=[db∧] giving first-order lifts, and the final t_it_jt_k pairing argument.
main_claim: There is a compact oriented smooth 4-manifold E with immersed disks f_i and framed algebraically dual immersed spheres g_i (λ(f_i,g_j)=δ_ij, λ(g_i,g_j)=0, μ̃(g_i)=0) for which no pairwise disjoint locally flat disks with the same boundaries and framings exist. This would disprove the unrestricted (good-group-free) disk embedding conjecture. The proof route: hypothetical disks ⇒ cuts of a plumbing into vertex pieces A,B joined by edges Y_i, with conjugated Brunnian three-slot laws holding at A and B ⇒ SL2 Chern–Simons edge potentials and complementary vertex graphs ⇒ triple-product gradient-ideal memberships ⇒ contradiction via a Koszul/Frobenius tensor argument in large characteristic.
sibling_notes: The sibling (rank 217, boundary-only obstruction) reported no_gap_found and also flagged the CS/deformation identities as the place most needing expert scrutiny. This paper shares the geometric reduction (Sec. 1) and the edge Chern–Simons machinery (Sec. 3–4). Its finish differs: a tensor/Koszul obstruction over T=K[t_i]/(t_i^2) with m≥5 active edges, using conjugated laws whose 9 Ad(g_ab) matrices span End(g). I found no failing step in that shared material either. The highest-risk unverified input for both papers is the appendix comparison of PTVV shifted forms with the strict trace form.
